text:
maria: heads-up — nightly RAG QA run flagged a large spike in bad answers for the 'customer-faq' prompt set. recall down ~18% vs baseline, but top-k reranked results look... oddly duplicated. attaching one example below.

aj: can you paste the query + top hits?

maria: sure — query: "how do I rotate API keys for a service account?"
results (id | score):
```
q1 -> doc_712 | 0.87
q1 -> doc_712_copy | 0.86   # near duplicate, different id but same text
q1 -> doc_189 | 0.71
q1 -> doc_045 | 0.32
```

sam: hmm odd. duplicates with different ids suggests indexing or chunking bug, or embed collisions. did anything change to the index or embedding pipeline recently?

maria: we onboarded embed-model-v2-quant last week and reindexed overnight. also changed FAISS config to use IVF-PQ with 256 clusters.

nora: eval-bot shows this started exactly after the reindex job 03:12 UTC.

eval-bot: nightly-eval | suite=rag_qa | baseline_recall=0.84 | current_recall=0.69 | anomalies=42 | cluster=eng-eu | reindex_job=2026-03-18T03:12:05Z

aj: two suspects: quantized model producing very similar vectors for near-duplicate chunks, or PQ/OPQ transform introduced rotation causing collisions. can we diff mean/var of embeddings before vs after?

sam: I dumped 10000 sample embeddings and ran PCA — principal directions rotated substantially, and pairwise cosine dist median dropped from 0.43 -> 0.27. that's consistent with vectors collapsing.

maria: is this more likely the quantized model or the post-processing (OPQ/normalize) step?

aj: OPQ can rotate space aggressively. if PQ params mismatched to the embed distribution it compresses similarity. the quant model also can collapse magnitudes. need quick ablation: 1) reindex with non-OPQ IVF-PQ, 2) reindex with fp16 embeddings (no quant), 3) run reranker-only eval to see if reranker masks recall loss.

nora: I can spin a reindex job for (1) and (2) on a small shard. want results within 2 hours?

maria: yes please. also run a reranker-only pass so we can separate retrieval vs rerank. add a diff of unique doc ids returned.

infra-bot: created job job-idx-2039-smallshard (config: no-opq, pq=16, nlist=256). ETA ~75m.

sam: meanwhile I ran a quick human check on 20 failed queries — ~60% are duplicates with different ids or near-identical chunks. that points to index mapping/chunking as well. could be a tokenizer change in preprocessing when we regenerated chunks.

aj: good call. did we change chunk params in the ingest script? (chunk_size or overlap)

maria: i reverted the ingest commit history — no change to chunk_size. but embed-service image moved from tag embed-svc:stable->embed-svc:canary two days ago. that aligns with the model bring-up.

nora: plan: 1) run smallshard reindex (no OPQ) 2) run reindex with fp16 embeddings 3) run reranker-only eval 4) compare id sets + pairwise cos distributions 5) if smallshard looks good, schedule full rollback of OPQ step and hold embed canary.

aj: if rollback fixes it, we'll add a preflight PCA sanity check to the onboarding pipeline so we catch vector collapse earlier.

maria: thanks. i uploaded a short list of 30 canonical queries and their ground-truth ids to the thread: https://redwood.internal/s/shortlists/203987 — use for quick smoke.

infra-bot: job job-idx-2039-smallshard completed (duration 68m). artifacts: /artifacts/job-idx-2039/*.pkl

sam: preliminary numbers from smallshard: recall moved 0.71 -> 0.83 when OPQ disabled, cosine median restored to ~0.41. reranker-only pass shows modest boost but not full recovery, so retrieval was main issue.

maria: sounds like OPQ/PQ paramization introduced the rotation artifact. can we schedule full reindex without OPQ during low-traffic window tonight?

nora: yes, will schedule full reindex at 02:30 UTC and hold the embed-svc canary until we add PCA gate. I'll also add an alert if embedding pairwise median drops >0.05 vs baseline.

aj: filed a quick RFC: add PCA/variance checks + run smallshard profile step to onboarding docs. link: https://redwood.internal/rfc/emb-onboard-smoke

maria: great. thanks all — keeping this thread as the record. will post post-mortem if full reindex resolves it. :white_check_mark:
